cost: Unit-weight PAVA and soft threshold O(n) work/storage; sorted simplex and L1 projection O(n log n) work/O(n) storage. Length <=10^6 with fallible allocation.
description: Project finite vectors onto monotone, simplex and L1-ball constraints and apply the L1 proximal soft-threshold map.
forward: Project finite vectors onto monotone, simplex and L1-ball constraints and apply the L1 proximal soft-threshold map.

Outside the L1 ball, its projection equals signed simplex projection of magnitudes and soft threshold at the common active magnitude difference. Isotonic regression preserves total sum in real arithmetic; finite checks separately test residual prefixes. Residual-prefix evidence is in the leaf partition oracle; the parent harness checks totals, order, idempotence and selected normal-cone inequalities.
inverse: At the real-model level exclude KKT-incompatible outputs for the tagged convex set/proximal problem. At the native level exclude different rounded transitions and invalid accepted results; arithmetic/allocation errors are retained, and tolerance-sized feasibility deviations are not silently discarded.

For fixed convex set C and output y in C, compatible real inputs are y+N_C(y). Soft-threshold zero coordinate has input fiber [-lambda,lambda]; nonzero coordinate reconstructs x_i=y_i+lambda*sign(y_i). This many-to-one model does not uniquely invert rounded implementations.
limitations: Real normal-cone and KKT laws do not by themselves prove floating-point outputs. Simplex relative mass residual acceptance is <=64*n*EPSILON, not objective error. L1 may exceed radius within tolerance. Overflow/cancellation can reject mathematically solvable inputs.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
state: Real maps have unique minimizers and KKT conditions; native f64 routines preserve explicit validation and acceptance tolerances rather than universal exact feasibility.
